newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian jets to patrol coast, border.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian jets to patrol coast, border.

text.p: Cambodia on Wednesday formally took possession of the first two of six trainer jets purchased from Israel and said the aircraft would be used for coastal patrol and to protect the country's borders.

Israel Aircraft Industry (IAI) representatives handed over the Czech-made L39 Albatrosses under a $6.3 million deal that includes delivery of four more second-hand L39s, four refurbished MiG-21s of the Cambodian air force, spare parts and training.

"Two (L39s) have arrived and the four others will arrive by the end of March, early April, and the four MiGs will be coming by September," said Defence Secretary of State Ek Sereywath, who signed the acceptance certificates with IAI's Dory Weiss.

"We have to have a minimum so that Cambodia is equipped to face small incidents on the border," First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said, adding that his country could not compete with the big air forces of neighbouring Thailand and Vietnam.
He said the trainers, which can carry bombs and rockets and be used as close fire support aircraft, would also be used to deter smuggling of logs by sea or illegal fishing.
Pilots would also train in the L39s before graduating to the four MiG-21 interceptors, which are receiving Western avionics systems in Israel.
"This is more important than the MiG, because this is for ground attack," Air Force Chief Major General Norodom Vatvani said of the L39, adding: "The MiG is just for prestige."

Ranariddh said the planes would not be used against an estimated 2,000 Khmer Rouge guerrillas still holding out against the coalition government despite the defection of thousands of their colleagues in the Maoist-inspired movement since August.
Two senior defectors from the Khmer Rouge, Sok Pheap and Ei Chien, attended the ceremony.
The air force has about 40 aircraft, including helicopters, while none of its former fleet of MiGs are beyond repair after years of neglect.
